operations.description: Generate an owned indexed-triangle closed annular solid from explicit inner and outer radii, two axial planes, angular subdivision, and a required face budget. It retains local positions, flat unit normals, face kinds, and angular-cell identity; it does not draw.

outerRadius.description: Finite caller local outer radius, strictly greater than innerRadius.

innerRadius.description: Finite caller local hole radius, strictly positive and less than outerRadius.

bottomZ.description: Finite caller local lower axial coordinate, strictly less than topZ.

topZ.description: Finite caller local upper axial coordinate, strictly greater than bottomZ.

slices.description: Angular cell count. This floor(INT_MAX/24) ceiling is representational only, not a useful-resolution or allocation promise.

maxFaces.description: Required caller face-work limit. Its signed-int packed-representation ceiling is not a practical-work or artistic recommendation.

positions.description: Owned local [x,y,z] vertices in outerBottom, outerTop, innerBottom, innerTop ring order, each ring in increasing cell order.

normals.description: Owned local flat unit [x,y,z] normals aligned one-to-one with triangles.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, including wrong passive carrier/keys, bool numeric, outerRadius<=innerRadius, innerRadius<=0, bottomZ>=topZ, slices outside3..89478485, or maxFaces outside1..715827881.
errors.FACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: Complete static input is valid but exact preallocation face count F=8*slices exceeds required maxFaces. No geometry/output allocation or partial result occurs.
errors.MESH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: Generated face has nonfinite edge component, zero edge scale, or zero rounded scaled cross. error_detail has faceIndex and edge,edge_scale,or cross_scale stage; no output is returned.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite nonnegative safe integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Representable index is outside the requested retained array range.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: An Into destination/offset does not provide three writable slots of the required native element type.

errorOrder: INVALID_INPUT during complete static input validation
FACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED after static validation and exact count calculation, before geometry allocation
MESH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID during canonical face-normal traversal after topology/positions are generated
INVALID_INDEX, INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, INVALID_OUTPUT during retained-result access in that order

behavior.input: Input has exactly outerRadius,innerRadius,bottomZ,topZ,slices,maxFaces. Static validation order is outer passive record/exact keys; outerRadius; innerRadius and outerRadius>innerRadius>0; bottomZ; topZ and bottomZ<topZ; slices; maxFaces. Every accepted number is finite binary64 and never bool. Integral slices/maxFaces carriers validate their stated domains before narrowing. Normalize accepted zeros to +0. No default, sort, callback, contour interpolation, renderer, or later-field short circuit. Complete static validation precedes count capacity, allocation, topology, and normal arithmetic.
behavior.counts_and_layout: Let S=slices. Compute F=8*S and V=4*S with exact wide integer arithmetic after static validation and before geometry allocation. FACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED if F>maxFaces. S<=89478485=floor(2147483647/24) keeps positions packed as 3*V and topology/normal arrays within signed-int addressability; F<=715827880. maxFaces may be715827881 but cannot authorize more than the operation's representable F. These values do not guarantee allocation success, latency, or a useful artistic range. Host resource allocation failure returns no result and is never INVALID_INPUT or partial success. Core retained work/storage is O(S), indexed reads O(1), detached export O(V+F).
behavior.topology: Local axis is Z. Angles increase from +X toward +Y. Set TAU=6.283185307179586 and evaluate theta=(TAU*cell)/slices in increasing cell order using named-target binary64 trigonometry. Position=(radius*cos(theta),radius*sin(theta),z). Append four shared rings in this order: outerBottom, outerTop, innerBottom, innerTop. Each ring appends S vertices in increasing cell order; no 2pi seam vertex is evaluated or stored. For each cell in increasing order, next=(cell+1) moduloS. Visit face kinds outer-wall, inner-wall, top-annulus, bottom-annulus. Their ordered quad perimeters are respectively (outerBottom/current,outerBottom/next,outerTop/next,outerTop/current), (innerBottom/current,innerTop/current,innerTop/next,innerBottom/next), (outerTop/current,outerTop/next,innerTop/next,innerTop/current), and (outerBottom/current,innerBottom/current,innerBottom/next,outerBottom/next). Every quad(a,b,c,d) appends triangles(a,b,c),(a,c,d). This gives outward wall normals, +Z top normals, -Z bottom normals, a welded angular seam, and no interior radial faces.
behavior.normals: For each ordered triangle(a,b,c) after positions/topology are generated, calculate u=b-a and v=c-a componentwise in x/y/z order. Reject a nonfinite edge component with MESH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID stage edge. Let su=max(abs(ux),abs(uy),abs(uz)) and sv likewise; reject zero su or sv at stage edge_scale. Divide every u component directly by su and every v component directly by sv. Compute qRaw=cross(uScaled,vScaled) through separate binary64 multiply/subtract operations in x/y/z order, no FMA or reassociation. Let sn=max(abs(qRaw.x),abs(qRaw.y),abs(qRaw.z)); reject zero sn at stage cross_scale. Divide qRaw directly by sn, then length=sqrt((qx*qx+qy*qy)+qz*qz); normal=q/length componentwise. Canonicalize completed zeros. No epsilon, analytic normal, binary32 narrowing, smooth interpolation, or silent dropped face is permitted. Dynamic failure returns no result and carries faceIndex/stage. The selected algorithm does not claim all-finite robustness.
behavior.ownership: Result stores packed owned primitive data and never retains caller record containers. Inputs are passive immutable interchange during eager generation. Result is immutable. vertexAt, triangleAt and normalAt return fresh triples; faceKindAt and cellAt are direct retained reads; toValues deep-copies exactly output_schema. vertexInto, triangleInto, and normalInto validate all access and destination conditions before three writes; failure leaves destination unchanged and successful writes leave slots outside the target triple unchanged. Materialization allocation failure does not corrupt retained data. No config serialization/replay, aliases, callbacks, iterator inputs, or draw side effect.
behavior.access: vertexCount() and faceCount() return retained counts. vertexAt, triangleAt and normalAt return fresh three-element carriers; faceKindAt and cellAt return aligned scalar data. Index must be finite safe nonnegative integer<=9007199254740991 and never bool; integral floating indices are accepted by dynamic-language targets. INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, which precedes INVALID_OUTPUT for vertexInto, triangleInto and normalInto. Each Into offset is finite safe nonnegative integral and the destination provides three writable slots of its required native element type: binary64 for vertex/normal, integer for triangle. Rejected reads leave every destination slot unchanged; success leaves slots outside the target triple unchanged. Java uses typed required int offsets and returns void; wrong/unrepresentable typed Java calls are host-call errors. JavaScript returns its destination and Python returns None. Deferred target bindings follow native_forms and native_types; no support is claimed before implementation and native validation.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.mesh.AnnularMesh3D.generate(Object config) returns AnnularMesh3D with vertexCount(), faceCount(), vertexAt(Object or long), triangleAt(Object or long), normalAt(Object or long), faceKindAt(Object or long), cellAt(Object or long), vertexInto(Object or long,double[],int), triangleInto(Object or long,int[],int), normalInto(Object or long,double[],int), and toValues(). No typed factory, aliases, presets, callbacks, iterator forms, or configuration serializer are proposed initially. Deferred JavaScript bindings use the same camelCase member names; Python uses vertex_count, face_count, vertex_at, triangle_at, normal_at, face_kind_at, cell_at, vertex_into, triangle_into, normal_into and to_values. Factory export/module locations are deferred target packaging decisions, not extra operation semantics. All targets remain unimplemented and unvalidated.
behavior.native_types: Follow the retained-operation passive-carrier convention: Java accepts Map outer records; accepted Java numeric carriers are only Byte, Short, Integer, Long, Float and Double, rejecting BigInteger, BigDecimal and custom Number before conversion. Java At/Into numeric index overloads accept Object or long as listed; Java vertexInto/normalInto require double[] and triangleInto requires int[]. Deferred JavaScript accepts passive Object/null-prototype records and ordinary Arrays; Python accepts exact builtin dict with int/float but never bool. JavaScript vertex/normal destinations are Float64Array or writable ordinary Array; triangle destinations are Int32Array or writable ordinary Array. Python vertex/normal destinations are exact builtin list or array(d); triangle destinations are exact builtin list. Destination validation must precede writes, including writable-slot checks for ordinary JavaScript Arrays. Host geometry/renderer carriers, class instances, active getters/proxies and custom dynamic-language mapping containers are outside portable interchange.
behavior.units: Caller-defined local Cartesian distance units. Positions use [x,y,z] with +Z from bottomZ toward topZ and angular coordinates around Z from +X toward +Y. No canvas mapping, camera, object transform, clipping, style, palette, lighting setup, renderer, shader, texture, callback, preset, or drawing command is part of generation.
behavior.numerics: Specified basic arithmetic is IEEE754 binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even with separate operation rounding. TAU is the stated binary64 literal. No FMA, reassociation, binary32 conversion, RNG, host global state, implicit epsilon, smoothing or coordinate clamp. Input and completed output zeros canonicalize to +0. Topology, counts, face metadata, indices and same-runtime binary64 output bits compare exactly. Cross-runtime fixture positions and normals compare with a separately generated nonnegative absolute allowance per component and case. Zero allowances require exact reference bits; exported zero is always positive zero. Bounds derive from reference sin/cos widened by two adjacent binary64 values each way (clipped to [-1,1], theta zero exact) and interval propagation through specified arithmetic. Inconclusive bounds block fixture acceptance; no global epsilon, relative fallback or automatic expansion. This selected-case engineering envelope is not a universal host-trigonometry guarantee. Near-collapse arbitrary inputs can differ in success/error across runtimes; registered error witnesses must match exact code, faceIndex and stage. Same-target/runtime repeated generation matches retained bits, without requiring Python reference bits for nonzero-allowance values.
environment: IEEE754 binary64 basic arithmetic, round-to-nearest ties-to-even
Java/Android Math.sin, Math.cos and Math.sqrt; JavaScript Math.sin, Math.cos and Math.sqrt; Python math.sin, math.cos and math.sqrt. No implicit angle reduction.
behavior.complexity: O(S) eager retained geometry and face-normal generation, O(1) indexed reads, and O(V+F) detached export. Avoid per-face object/vector allocation in generation or ordinary drawing loops. The representational ceiling is not a memory or throughput promise.
behavior.native_errors: Static/access errors expose stable code. MESH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID also exposes faceIndex and stage, serialized as error_detail:{faceIndex,stage}. FACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED has no partial result. Host allocation/resource failure remains a host resource exception and is not converted to validation error. No renderer/adapter result is produced by core generation.

operations.description: Remap an owned packed ARGB8 raster through explicit source coordinates using edge-clamped bilinear interpolation.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed static configuration, wrong keys/carriers, nonpositive or nonintegral dimensions, pixel length/value violation, coordinate shape/value violation, nonfinite coordinate, or output coordinate-count mismatch.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Pixel index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Pixel index is representable but outside the retained output raster.

errorOrder: Validate top-level exact Map keys; source exact Map keys; source width, height and product; source pixel carrier/count then values in row order; outputWidth, outputHeight and product; sourceCoordinates carrier/count then each pair shape and x,y values in row order. Typed overload follows the corresponding dimension/product, pixel buffer/count, output dimension/product, coordinate buffer/count then finite XY order. All static errors are INVALID_INPUT; complete validation precedes output allocation and sampling.

behavior.input: Validate exactly source, outputWidth, outputHeight and sourceCoordinates. Source dimensions are positive integral values and pixels has exactly source.width*source.height unsigned32 values. The coordinate list has exactly outputWidth*outputHeight pairs, each finite binary64. Validate all static shape, dimensions, pixels and coordinates before output allocation or sampling. No defaults, modes or maxPixels.
behavior.sampling: For each row-major destination coordinate, clamp x and y independently to [0,width-1] and [0,height-1]. Let x0=floor(x), x1=min(x0+1,width-1), fx=x-x0 and likewise y0,y1,fy. Read four packed source pixels and interpolate A,R,G,B independently as straight stored ARGB8 channels: top=a+(b-a)*fx, bottom=c+(d-c)*fx, value=top+(bottom-top)*fy, with each operation separately rounded binary64. Clamp each value to [0,255], then compute floor(value+0.5) once and repack ARGB8. Integer coordinates preserve all 32 bits, including hidden RGB in transparent pixels. No FMA, intermediate integer lerps, gamma conversion or premultiplication.
behavior.ownership: The completed result owns a detached packed raster. It retains neither source pixels nor sourceCoordinates, and has no in-place form. Later caller mutation cannot affect the result. A failed call exposes no partial output.
behavior.access: width() and height() return dimensions. pixelAt(index) validates index as a finite safe nonnegative integer, then checks index < width*height; INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE. pixels() returns a detached int[] in Java (unsigned32 bit patterns), and toValues() returns detached {width,height,pixels}. Safe means at most 9007199254740991; negative zero is accepted as zero. pixelAt returns the Java int ARGB bit pattern; portable toValues pixels are unsigned32 numbers. Object indices accept only the same six numeric carriers as input.
behavior.typed_java: Java also accepts sourceW, sourceH, int[] sourcePixels, outW, outH and double[] packedXY. It executes the same kernel, validation order, interpolation and ownership semantics as the portable object form. Typed arrays use row-major pixels and x,y pairs.
behavior.numeric: Coordinates use caller-defined pixel-center units with top-left origin. Clamp whole coordinates before floor/fraction, including extreme finite coordinates. Basic arithmetic is IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even in the stated order; final channel quantization is floor(value+0.5).
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.raster.RasterRemap2D.remap(Object), the typed packed-buffer overload, width(), height(), pixelAt(Object or long), pixels(), and toValues(). Java-only implementation is pending; other targets remain deferred.
behavior.environment: No RNG, noise, time, renderer, host image, callback, color mode or third-party dependency is retained or consulted.
behavior.limits: Source width*height <= 2147483647; outputWidth*outputHeight <= 1073741823. Compute products without signed32 overflow and reject excess before buffer allocation. These are representation limits, not promised allocatable sizes; allocation failure is not INVALID_INPUT.
behavior.carriers: Java object records are Map with exact keys; arrays are List, coordinate pairs are List of exactly two elements. Numeric carriers are only Byte, Short, Integer, Long, Float and Double; reject boolean, strings, BigInteger, BigDecimal and arbitrary Number subclasses. Dimension and unsigned32 pixel values must be finite integral numbers in their bounds. Coordinates convert to finite double. Typed overload takes int dimensions, int[] pixels and double[] packedXY; reject null buffers. Passive stable inputs are assumed; concurrent caller mutation during a call is outside contract.

operations.description: Generate retained ordered integer-cell rectangles by attempt-bounded binary cuts with random or longer-axis selection.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Invalid configuration carrier, keys or values.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Negative or greater-than-safe-integer index.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Valid numeric index outside retained sequence.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: Null or non-length4 destination; index checked first, no partial writes.

behavior.generation: Private seeded ordered live-leaf selection, RANDOM or LONGEST axis, failed unit-axis attempts consume no cut; successful cuts cover every interior integer boundary under unit mapping; remove parent preserving survivors then append low/high children. Exact consumption and arithmetic in normative contract.
behavior.environment: Private xoshiro128**1.1/SplitMix64 as seeded-quadrant-partition; no host globals, renderer, time or assets.
behavior.ownership: Immutable retained values; copied exports; boundsInto validates before allocation-free writes.
behavior.complexity: O(attempts*maximumLiveCount) worst-case work; O(finalLiveCount) storage; grow by actual successes. Representation bounds are not memory promises.

operations.description: Clip supplied segments to a simple concave polygon, retaining source identity and every positive-length interior or boundary interval.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Static shape/carrier/domain failure.
errors.OUTPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: Next retained interval exceeds output allowance.
errors.REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE: Positive exact interval or exterior gap cannot be represented distinctly; sourceIndex,intervalIndex,stage.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Invalid numeric index.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Valid index outside result.

behavior.input: Exactly polygon,segments,maxWork,maxOutputSegments in a passive record. Validate record/keys, polygon list and each finite pair in order, segments list and every finite quadruple in order, maxWork, maxOutputSegments. All numeric carriers are finite binary64 and never bool; integer limits require exact integral values in schema domain. Java accepts Byte,Short,Integer,Long,Float,Double only. Normalize signed zero. Complete all static validation before work/topology. No implicit defaults or closed-vertex duplicate removal.
behavior.work: V=polygon.length,S=segments.length. Compute W=V*V+S*(8*V*V+16*V+8) in exact integers. WORK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED iff W>maxWork, before topology testing or generated output allocation. W is a conservative abstract geometry allowance, not milliseconds, bytes or literal bigint operation count. Empty sources still pay V². Big-integer costs and host allocation are not covered by a timing guarantee.
behavior.polygon: At least3 distinct vertices, implicit last-to-first closure, exact nonzero signed area. Reject repeated vertices including a closing duplicate, adjacent collinear backtracking/overlap, or any nonadjacent edge contact/crossing. Straight collinear continuation is accepted. Either winding and concavity accepted. Exact dyadic arithmetic over input binary64 values; no epsilon. INVALID_POLYGON after work preflight.
behavior.clipping: Visit sources in input order. Zero-length source contributes nothing. For nonzero segment A+t(B-A), collect exact t=0,1 and each segment-edge intersection whose exact t,u are closed[0,1]. For collinear edges include edge endpoint t values within[0,1]. Parallel noncollinear edges add none. Sort/deduplicate exact rationals. Classify each open interval by its exact rational midpoint: retain iff inside or on boundary using exact even-odd containment. Merge neighboring retained intervals sharing an exact parameter. Never bridge a positive exterior interval. Point-only contacts are omitted.
behavior.rounding: Traverse merged intervals in increasing t. Before conversion check retained count against maxOutputSegments, otherwise OUTPUT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with sourceIndex and intervalIndex. Convert each t and exact A+t(B-A) coordinate once to binary64 nearest-even, canonical +0. t=0/1 keeps the corresponding input endpoint except zero normalization. No intermediate binary64 interpolation. REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE stages in order: parameter if rounded t0>=t1; endpoints if rounded coordinate pairs coincide; gap if previous returned interval of this source has rounded end>=current rounded start despite positive exact gap. Error detail sourceIndex,intervalIndex,stage. No returned partial result. Rounded endpoints may lie slightly off the exact boundary; centerline clipping does not constrain rendered stroke width. sourceIndex and intervalIndex are zero-based; intervalIndex counts merged retained intervals within that source before output conversion.
behavior.ownership: Retain owned packed coordinates, source indices and rounded parameter pairs only; do not retain inputs, exact rational temporaries or a renderer. Into reads allocate no result storage; At/export return detached data. No mutation or retained region session. Host allocation failure remains host failure.
behavior.access: size() counts retained segments. segmentAt(index) and segmentInto(index,output,offset) use4 doubles; intervalAt and intervalInto use2 doubles; sourceIndexAt returns integer. toValues returns output-schema keys in segments,sourceIndices,intervals order and detached nested lists. Index finite nonnegative safe integer<=9007199254740991; INVALID_INDEX before INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE before INVALID_OUTPUT. Java Object and long indices accepted; offsets required int. All destination slots remain unchanged on validation failure.
behavior.complexity: Correctness baseline O(V²+S*V²) geometric work plus sorting and exact arithmetic costs; O(V+S+K) retained input/output scale with per-source O(V) cut storage, K retained intervals. Packed segment quadruples bound maxOutputSegments by floor(INT_MAX/4); count ceilings are representational, not recommended use.

operations.description: Retain a closed uniform Catmull-Rom spline from explicit planar controls with direct parameter and approximate distance queries.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed static carrier/key/value, fewer than three controls, invalid subdivision or representation bound.
errors.INVALID_QUERY: Malformed query, mode/value, nonfinite scalar or invalid target.
errors.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: Nonfinite computed creation or query intermediate; no partial result.

behavior.creation: Create from exactly {controls,subdivisions}. Controls is an ordered list of N exact [x,y] pairs, N>=3, finite binary64 coordinates in caller drawing units. R is an integer>=1, the number of equal-parameter chords in each control-to-control span. Both are required; no defaults or encouraged artistic ranges. Validate top-level keys, control count, R and product bounds before coordinates in row order, x then y. N<=268435455 permits packed8N coefficient storage; N*R<=2147483646 permits a signed32 indexed cumulative table of N*R+1 entries. These are representation bounds, not allocation promises. A nonfinite computed intermediate raises NUMERIC_OVERFLOW without exposing a curve. Duplicate and all-coincident controls are allowed; no sorting, removal or zero-chord pruning.
behavior.arithmetic: All primitives separately round IEEE754 binary64 nearest ties-to-even; no FMA, reassociation or extended intermediates. For span i, p0=control[(i-1+N)%N], p1=control[i], p2=control[(i+1)%N], p3=control[(i+2)%N], independently for x and y: a=0.5*(((-p0+3*p1)-3*p2)+p3); b=0.5*(((2*p0-5*p1)+4*p2)-p3); c=0.5*(-p0+p2); d=p1; position(t)=((a*t+b)*t+c)*t+d; tangent(t)=(3*a*t+2*b)*t+c. Check every primitive result for finiteness. At t=0 return p1 exactly and tangent c; at t=1 advance to the next span and use its t=0 rule. Canonicalize exposed zeros to +0.
behavior.table: Use fdlibm5.3 StrictMath.hypot. Build cumulative[0]=0; for each span i, start at control[i], evaluate j=1..R at binary64 j/R (j=R uses the exact endpoint rule), measure each chord from the preceding sample, and add its length to the running total. Retain every running total in span/subdivision order, including zero chords and rounded plateaus. Final total is approximate arc length, not analytically integrated perimeter.
behavior.queries: Validate query shape, mode, value and target before constant-curve shortcuts. Query mode is parameter or distance. Wrap finite v to period P using binary64 remainder truncated toward zero; if w<0 add P; if w==P or w==0 canonicalize +0. Parameter uses P=N, i=floor(w), t=w-i. Distance with length0 returns control0 and span0 tangent after validation. Otherwise wrap by P=length; w==0 uses span0,t=0 before any search. For w>0 use upper-bound search for largest cumulative[k]<=w, skipping equal plateaus; u=(w-cumulative[k])/(cumulative[k+1]-cumulative[k]); span=floor(k/R), local=(k%R+u)/R, then evaluate the cubic, using the endpoint rule when local==1. Nonfinite query intermediates raise NUMERIC_OVERFLOW; no partial output.
behavior.native_surface: Java org.procedurals.paths.ClosedSpline2D.create(Object) and create(double[][] controls,int subdivisions) share validation and one kernel. serialize() returns detached {controls,subdivisions}. sampleParameter(double) and sampleDistance(double) return immutable Sample with x(),y(),tangentX(),tangentY(); target-array overloads write exactly four entries [x,y,tangentX,tangentY] without allocation. sample(Object) accepts exactly {mode,value} and returns {point:[x,y],tangent:[dx,dy]}. length(), controlCount() and subdivisions() expose metadata. No generic callbacks or mutable buffers.
behavior.ownership: Copy all inputs; no aliases are retained. Exports and Sample results are detached. Failed creation or query exposes no partial result. Work is O(N*R), retained storage O(N*R+N), parameter query O(1), distance query O(log(N*R)). No renderer, RNG, time or assets.
behavior.carriers: Object records use exact passive Map/List containers. Java numeric carriers are Byte, Short, Integer, Long, Float and Double; reject null, boolean, strings, arrays in object route, arbitrary Number subclasses, BigInteger and BigDecimal. Typed arrays are copied. Validate target-array scalar then target and calculate into locals; errors never partially modify target.
behavior.normative_contract: design/operations/closed-spline-contract.md is normative for precise validation order, arithmetic, endpoint/plateau decisions and atomic target writes.

operations.description: Immutable ordered opaque sRGB8 palette sampled by a phase in cycles, with linear encoded-channel interpolation and fixed RGB24 quantization.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Invalid object keys, colors container/length, or any nonintegral, boolean, nonfinite or out-of-range RGB24 entry. No partial palette returned.
errors.INVALID_QUERY: Phase is not a permitted finite binary64 scalar. No partial output.

behavior.construction: Validate passive object with exactly colors; colors must be an array of 1..2147483647 mathematical integral values in 0..16777215. Integral floating values accepted; booleans rejected. Validate keys, array shape/length, then entries in order. Snapshot and retain supplied order including duplicates. Normalize zero to +0. No default palette. Serialize only {colors:[...]}, returning detached data each time.
behavior.query_validation: Query is one finite binary64 phase scalar. Reject bool, null, string, array, object and nonfinite values with INVALID_QUERY. Convert permitted native number to binary64 before validation; an overflowing Python integer is INVALID_QUERY. Validate even for a single-entry palette. Unsupported native call arity is a host-language call error, not an interchange-data result.
behavior.wrapping: Let n be palette length. Compute f=phase-floor(phase) as one separately rounded binary64 subtraction. Normalize f==0 to +0. If f==1 from rounding a tiny negative phase, set f=0. Compute x=f*n as one separately rounded binary64 multiplication; if x==n set x=0. Let i=floor(x), t=x-i (separately rounded), j=0 if i+1==n else i+1. Never cast the unwrapped phase to an integer index. All finite phases are valid; large phases may lose all fractional precision and sample the first entry. No epsilon or reflection/absolute value. Integer-shift periodicity is guaranteed only when the shifted binary64 phase preserves the fractional part.
behavior.color: Entries and result are unsigned RGB24 integers 0xRRGGBB, with each encoded sRGB8 channel in 0..255. Interpolate encoded channels directly; no gamma decode, HSB conversion, alpha, premultiplication or host colorMode. For each R,G,B channel a,b: d=b-a; p=t*d; v=a+p; q=floor(v+0.5), every arithmetic step separately rounded binary64. Pack qR*65536+qG*256+qB as an exact integer. No FMA/reassociation; IEEE round-to-nearest ties-to-even for primitive operations, explicit final half-up channel quantization. Result integer compares exactly, including canonical positive zero. With one entry return its value after validating the phase.
behavior.ownership: No mutable input/output alias or externally observable cache. Reordered/repeated queries and interleaved palettes produce the same values. Native scalar query returns a colour value and requires no query-container allocation. Caller mutation of serialized colors does not affect the palette.
behavior.environment: No RNG, noise, time, rendering, assets, global colour state or implicit seed. Opacity is caller mark style. Renderer adapters must explicitly convert RGB24 to their native colour representation; this contract does not validate any adapter.
behavior.cost: O(n) validation and snapshot storage at construction and serialization; O(1) bounded work per query. No eager sampled ramp. Length representability does not promise an allocation succeeds on a particular machine; ordinary resource exhaustion is not an INVALID_INPUT semantic error.
behavior.native_representations: Passive interchange data only, not callbacks/accessors/proxies. Java accepts boxed Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double and native double query; unsupported Number subclasses rejected before lossy coercion. Python accepts int/float but not bool; entries validated as mathematical integers before narrowing. JavaScript requires number. Native palette containers are Java List, JavaScript Array, and Python list/tuple; serialization is object/map with a newly owned list/array. No packed signed ARGB input or string hex parsing. Query schemas describe canonical binary64 interchange values after permitted native numeric normalization; raw JSON token parsing is outside this operation. A Python integer just above maximum binary64 may round to that finite maximum and is accepted, while an integer that overflows conversion is INVALID_QUERY. The schema is not a raw arbitrary-precision-token parser.
behavior.compatibility: Cycles, negative wrap and quantization are deliberate portable semantics. Source v/n conversion can alter floating arithmetic; no Processing lerpColor or source-pixel identity claim. Selected membership establishes the computation, not those exact native numerics.
behavior.native_api: Java org.procedurals.color.CyclicPalette.create(params), JavaScript cyclicPalette(params), Python cyclic_palette(params), each returning immutable sampler with sample(phase) and serialize(). Java may overload sample(Object) and sample(double) for dynamic validation and scalar hot path. Native error classes expose code; no alternate coordinate mode or alias factory.

operations.description: Produce owned exact planar Delaunay topology from an ordered finite binary64 site list and explicit deterministic work budget. It computes canonical unique vertices, input mappings, positive indexed faces, unique edges and final face incidence only; it has no random stream, renderer, palette, clipping, site sampler or draw side effect.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, wrong passive carrier/keys/shape, bool numeric, invalid point count or invalid maxWork. It has no dynamic detail.
errors.WORK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: A charged canonicalize, hull_lower, hull_upper, locate or legalize step would exceed maxWork. error_detail is {workUsed,stage}; it exposes no partial topology.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: An indexed access index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: A representable index is outside the relevant retained input, vertex, face or edge range.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: An Into destination or offset cannot accept the complete requested carrier without mutation.

errorOrder: Complete static validation of points and maxWork yields INVALID_INPUT before budget checking, canonical point/map allocation, sorting, topology work or result exposure.
For each charged step, WORK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED precedes that step's predicate/topology mutation and leaves workUsed unchanged.
For every Into access, INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, which precedes INVALID_OUTPUT.

behavior.input: Input keys are exactly points and maxWork. points is an ordered passive list of finite binary64 [x,y] pairs of length 0..357913943. maxWork is a finite safe integer 0..9007199254740991. Booleans are not numbers. Validate all static input—including every point—before checking budget or copying topology. Normalize negative zero to positive zero. Any static violation raises INVALID_INPUT with no partial result. No defaults.
behavior.predicates: Use exact dyadic signs of the represented finite binary64 coordinates. Orientation(a,b,c) is sign((bx-ax)*(cy-ay)-(by-ay)*(cx-ax)). For incircle(a,b,c,d), set ax=a.x-d.x, ay=a.y-d.y and similarly bx,by,cx,cy, all as exact dyadic values. Its determinant is (ax*ax+ay*ay)*(bx*cy-by*cx) - (bx*bx+by*by)*(ax*cy-ay*cx) + (cx*cx+cy*cy)*(ax*by-ay*bx). For positively oriented a,b,c, positive means d strictly inside, zero cocircular, negative outside. Do not use collinear a,b,c as a circle test. No rounded floating-point subtraction/product, epsilon, lossy rescaling, FMA, jitter or supertriangle affects topology. A proved exact-sign fast path may be used only with identical signs.
behavior.canonicalization_and_output: Equal normalized coordinates collapse without tolerance. Unique points sort by numeric X then Y. For a face triple, reverse its final two vertices if orientation is negative, then cyclically rotate so its smallest index is first; zero orientation is never a face. New faces from one mutation are lexicographically sorted before appending to the active creation sequence; removal preserves the relative order of surviving faces. Final faces are lexicographically sorted. Build edges and final face incidences from that final order. Mathematical positive orientation appears clockwise on a screen with Y down. Every unique site participates for two-dimensional inputs; faces cover the convex hull without crossings, overlaps, zero-area faces or boundary clipping.
work_schedule: workUsed starts at zero. Before a charged step with cost c, if c>maxWork-workUsed, raise WORK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with workUsed and stage. The rejected step is not performed or charged; no partial mesh escapes. Stages are canonicalize, hull_lower, hull_upper, locate and legalize.

After complete static validation, charge N units atomically at canonicalize, before owned point/map buffers and canonical sorting. Empty input costs zero. A budget smaller than N therefore fails with workUsed=0. This accounts for input-sized preprocessing; sorting itself is not charged per comparison and must be O(N log N), not quadratic.

If U<3, finish immediately. Otherwise build lower and upper monotone hull chains, respectively visiting canonical vertex indices ascending and descending. While a chain has at least two vertices, charge one at its hull stage and test orientation(lastButOne,last,new). If sign<=0, pop last and continue; otherwise stop. Append new. Form strict CCW hull by concatenating lower without its last vertex and upper without its last vertex. Collinear sites are excluded from this corner hull, not discarded from input. If hull has fewer than three corners, finish with empty faces/edges.

Form the positive corner fan from the first hull vertex to each consecutive pair of later hull vertices. Canonicalize and sort these initial faces to form the initial active sequence. This linear construction adds no separate charge.

Visit all unique non-corner sites in canonical order. Scan active faces in creation order. For each visited face charge one at locate, then evaluate all three oriented-edge signs against the site. A containing face has all signs>=0. Stop at the first containing face; do not inspect every later face. If all signs>0, replace this face by its three site-connected faces. If one sign is zero, use the incidence map for that edge to replace its one or two faces by two or four faces respectively. Distinct sites cannot equal an existing vertex; two zero signs therefore cannot occur here. Remove old faces, canonicalize and lexsort all replacements, and append them. Incidence lookup/mutation is local; no full-face-list rebuilding after each insertion.

Only after all site insertions, initialize the legalization queue with every internal edge. The queue is a set with lexicographic minimum extraction: an endpoint pair occurs at most once while queued. Each extraction costs one at legalize before removing it. An absent or now-boundary edge still costs its extraction and does nothing. Endpoint-pair identity is geometric, so a pair removed and recreated before extraction refers to its current incidence.

For a current internal edge (u<v), let a be its opposite vertex to the left of oriented u->v and b the opposite vertex to the right. It is flippable only if u and v lie strictly on opposite sides of oriented a->b. Otherwise do nothing. Test incircle(u,v,a,b), whose first triple is positive. Flip if the sign is positive; if zero, flip only when sorted(a,b) is lexicographically smaller than (u,v). Negative does nothing. A flip replaces its two faces with the two faces around diagonal a,b, canonically appended as above. Add every edge of both new faces that is currently internal to the queue, including the new diagonal, suppressing already-queued pairs. No global re-enqueue pass.

On empty queue, finish canonical output and return workUsed. Final sorting and incidence materialization add no separate charge and must be O(U log U). A locate unit uses three orientation signs; a legalization unit uses a bounded number of orientation/incircle signs and constant local topology updates plus O(log U) queue work. Exact integer operands have finite binary64-derived bit limits. The input charge covers linear storage and O(N log N) sorting; this is a deterministic computation budget, not bytes or elapsed time. No uncharged global rescanning is permitted inside a local flip. Active face scanning is charged face by face, so long location searches cannot evade the budget.
behavior.limits: 357913943 is a conservative input representation ceiling so N distinct sites fit packed signed-int-indexed arrays: F<=2U-5 implies 3F<=2147483647 and E<=3U-6 implies 2E<=2147483647. It is not an artistic recommendation, allocation guarantee, latency guarantee, runtime guarantee or measured heap bound. maxWork is a separate caller computation budget. Allocation failure remains a host resource failure, never INVALID_INPUT or empty success.
behavior.ownership: Successful output owns detached packed data and retains no caller record/list, predicate state, work-budget object, renderer, style, RNG state or callback. Caller mutation after return cannot change the result. All static validation completes before output-sized allocation. Getter/export allocation failure leaves an existing result usable. No serialize/toJSON/config echo or partial result exists.

Every index must be a finite safe nonnegative integer <=9007199254740991, never bool. INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, which precedes INVALID_OUTPUT for Into. Java Object and long overloads share this validation, including the safe-integer ceiling. At returns fresh detached carriers. Into validates index, destination native type, nonnegative integral offset and enough space for the complete carrier before writing; failure preserves every destination slot, success preserves slots outside the carrier. Use overflow-safe remaining-capacity checks. Java typed int offsets and wrong/unrepresentable typed calls are host-call behavior; Java Into returns void, deferred JavaScript returns destination, Python returns None.

Factory export/module locations remain target packaging choices. No aliases, callbacks, iterator, configuration serializer or draw API.

Reject BigInteger, BigDecimal and custom Number before conversion. Coordinates convert once to finite binary64; integral fields/indices must satisfy their exact stated domain before narrowing. Validate destination slot writability before writes. No active getters/proxies, host geometry input, native typed-array input pairs, class instances or custom dynamic-language mappings/lists. Java containers must be passive and unchanged during the call.
environment: exact finite binary64 dyadic orientation and incircle signs
no host RNG, noise, renderer, time, font, asset or third-party geometry dependency
behavior.complexity: N is original input count, U canonical unique count, F final face count, E final edge count. Static validation is O(N) before budget checking and uses no retained input-sized coordinate or map buffers. Sorting is O(N log N). The charged schedule covers N canonicalization work, hull predicate visits, face-by-face location scans and legalization queue extractions. Live topology and its queue require O(U+F+E) storage; reclaim removed faces rather than retaining an ever-growing history. Retained result and detached export are O(N+U+F+E), including inputToVertex of length N. Indexed reads are O(1). This is work accounting and asymptotic storage, not a measured performance claim.
behavior.units: Caller-defined Cartesian distance units for [x,y]. Positive orientation follows mathematical +X/right, +Y/up convention; the same triples appear clockwise when drawn directly on a Y-down screen. No coordinate transformation, clipping, canvas size, angle parameter or renderer state is implicit.
behavior.native_errors: Static/access exceptions expose stable code. WORK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED also exposes long workUsed and String stage, serialized as error_detail:{workUsed,stage}. No partial result. Host allocation failures stay host resource exceptions. Impossible mesh states are implementation defects, not expected contract errors or empty successes.

operations.description: An immutable seeded single-octave 2D gradient field with pure binary64 samples in [0,1]. Independently specified; not Processing noise compatibility.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Wrong constructor shape, unknown/missing key, bool/nonfinite/noninteger seed, or seed outside unsigned32.
errors.INVALID_QUERY: Query not exactly two finite numbers, or either floor(q) or floor(q)+1 outside safe integer range.

behavior.construction: Validate exactly one seed key and mathematical integral value 0..4294967295. Integral floating values allowed, booleans rejected. Detach input; store immutable seed, normalize zero to +0. Serialize only {seed}; no derived table, cache or query history.
behavior.query_validation: Interchange query is exactly [x,y]. Validate shape then x then y. Both finite binary64 values must satisfy -9007199254740991 <= q < 9007199254740991, so floor(q) and floor(q)+1 are exact safe integers. Return no partial output on error. Native hot path sample(x,y) takes scalars and does not allocate a query tuple. The same native sample method may accept one coordinate tuple for interchange or two scalar arguments for the hot path. Invalid tuple shape is INVALID_QUERY. Unsupported native call arity is a host-language call error and is not an interchange-data result.
behavior.cells: I=floor(x), J=floor(y), retained as exact integers for corner arithmetic. u=x-floor(x), v=y-floor(y) each separately rounded binary64 subtraction. Tiny negative inputs may produce u or v equal to 1 by rounding; do not correct/reject. For hashing only, reduce each I+di,J+dj modulo 2^32. Do not cast a binary64 floor directly to signed int32; Java may convert to long then take low32 bits.
behavior.mix32: For unsigned32 v, in order: v=v XOR (v logical-right-shift 16); v=(v*0x7feb352d) modulo 2^32; v=v XOR (v logical-right-shift 15); v=(v*0x846ca68b) modulo 2^32; return v XOR (v logical-right-shift 16). Every integer multiply and XOR retains exactly 32 bits.
behavior.corner_hash: For integer corner (i,j): a=mix32(seed XOR u32(i) XOR 0x9e3779b9); h=mix32(a XOR u32(j) XOR 0x85ebca6b). Gradient index=h AND 7. u32 is mathematical modulo 2^32.
behavior.dot: gx*dx rounded to px; gy*dy rounded to py; px+py rounded to result. No gradient normalization. Corner order n00,n10,n01,n11 with offsets (u,v),(u-1,v),(u,v-1),(u-1,v-1); every offset subtraction separately rounded.
behavior.fade: F(t), consecutive binary64 steps: a=t*t; b=a*t; c=6*t; d=c-15; e=t*d; f=e+10; return b*f. No polynomial expansion, reassociation or FMA.
behavior.interpolation: L(a,b,t), consecutive binary64 steps: d=b-a; p=t*d; return a+p. Compute fx=F(u),fy=F(v); bottom=L(n00,n10,fx); top=L(n01,n11,fx); raw=L(bottom,top,fy); scaled=0.5*raw; result=0.5+scaled. Clamp only final result to [0,1], normalize zero to +0.
behavior.numerics: Every stated floating operation is IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even, separately rounded; no FMA or reassociation. Scalars compare exactly after canonical positive zero. No transcendental functions. Raw ideal bound [-1,1]; output closed interval [0,1], both endpoints possible; lattice samples exactly 0.5.
behavior.state: Pure immutable field. No RNG stream, table shuffle, host noise, time, assets, renderer, or externally mutable state. Queries may be repeated/reordered and distinct fields interleaved without changing results. Seed changes field identity; no statistical independence or cryptographic guarantee.
behavior.periodicity: Each lattice axis repeats at 2^32. Sample equality under a shifted coordinate requires that shift and fractional part be exactly representable and both queries in domain. Large coordinates lose subcell resolution; no epsilon correction. No configurable seamless tiling API.
behavior.cost: O(1) storage and query work: four corner hashes, at most eight mix32 evaluations (pure common-subexpression reuse is permitted), four dot products, fixed fades/lerps. Native sample(x,y) avoids query-array allocation. No eager full-grid sampling or hidden unbounded cache.
behavior.native_representations: Passive interchange data only, not active callbacks/accessors/proxies. Java accepts boxed Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double or native double scalars; unsupported Number subclasses are rejected before lossy coercion. Python accepts int/float but never bool; coordinates convert to binary64 before domain validation. JavaScript requires number scalars. Preserve seed integer semantics before conversion; constructor/serialization field names remain seed.

operations.description: Immutable seeded single-octave three-coordinate gradient field with pure binary64 samples in[0,1]; independent of Processing noise.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Wrong constructor shape, unknown/missing key, bool/nonfinite/noninteger seed, or seed outside unsigned32.
errors.INVALID_QUERY: Query not exactly three finite supported numbers, or a coordinate outside the safe-corner domain.

behavior.identity: Required uint32 seed, immutable detached serialization; pure x/y/z queries with no global state or sample consumption.
behavior.numerics: Exact binary64 safe-corner subtraction, three-stage lowbias32 corner hash, twelve integer gradients, quintic fades and x-then-y-then-z interpolation; clamp output0..1. See normative document for exact order.
behavior.native: GradientNoise3D01.create(Object) or create(long); serialize; sample(Object tuple), sample(Object,Object,Object), sample(double,double,double); only six standard boxed numeric carriers.
behavior.complexity: O(1) storage and eight-corner work per sample; scalar hot path allocation-free.

operations.description: Retain a finite two-dimensional trajectory by sampling an explicit gradient field at each evolving position and advancing a fixed distance. Reuse its positions and headings for different marks.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, including layout-unsafe steps.
errors.TRACE_QUERY_INVALID: Dynamic field coordinate invalid; stepIndex and query_x/query_y stage.
errors.TRACE_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: Dynamic nonfinite heading/displacement/endpoint; stepIndex and stated stage.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Representable index exceeds point or heading range.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: pointInto storage/offset is not writable binary64 space for two values.

behavior.input: Interchange input is exactly the eight required keys. Passive JSON-compatible records only. Validate outer shape/keys, field shape/seed, start shape and x/y values, steps, stepDistance, fieldScale, fieldOffset shape and x/y values, angleBase, angleScale in that order. Every numeric value must be finite; booleans are never numbers. Integral floating counts/seeds are allowed. Steps must be0..1073741822 inclusive and stepDistance>=0. Copy configuration, canonicalizing every zero to positive zero.
behavior.construction: An explicit eager trace call authorizes O(steps) work and retained allocation. Configuration validation never samples or allocates output-sized storage. Complete all static validation before array allocation or field sampling. Reconstruct the existing GradientNoise2D01 from detached seed configuration. The first public form takes the complete interchange configuration; no arbitrary field callback or second field carrier is accepted.
behavior.layout: N=steps. Privately retain2*(N+1) binary64 position coordinates and N binary64 headings. Positions[0] is start; heading[i] drives the movement positions[i]→positions[i+1]. Count bound N<=1073741822 ensures2*(N+1)<=2147483647. This is a shared index representation bound, not a promise that maximal allocation succeeds. No extra maxSteps/maxBytes input. Incidental host allocation failure returns no result and remains a host resource exception, never INVALID_INPUT or partial successful output.
behavior.advance: For i=0..N-1: qx=round64(x*fieldScale), then qx=round64(qx+fieldOffset.x); validate qx in the field query domain before computing qy the same way. Sample field(qx,qy). mapped=round64(angleScale*sample); heading=round64(angleBase+mapped), then canonicalize a zero heading to positive zero. dx=round64(stepDistance*hostCos(heading)); dy=round64(stepDistance*hostSin(heading)). nextX=round64(x+dx); nextY=round64(y+dy). Canonicalize completed zero coordinates to positive zero, store point[i+1] and heading[i], and feed those stored coordinates into the next iteration. No FMA, reassociation, angle reduction, clamping, closure or binary32 conversion.
behavior.dynamic_validation: Per step, validate finite multiply and sum for query_x and its existing noise domain -9007199254740991<=qx<9007199254740991, then query_y similarly. Query failures use TRACE_QUERY_INVALID with zero-based stepIndex and stage query_x/query_y. After sampling check mapped and heading finite (stage heading), then cosine and dx finite (delta_x), sine and dy finite (delta_y), then nextX finite (position_x), nextY finite (position_y). These use TRACE_ARITHMETIC_INVALID with stepIndex/stage. Discard internal partial arrays and return no path. Final endpoint is not sampled to validate a hypothetical next step.
behavior.zero: N=0 validates every static input but performs no field query, arithmetic advance or trigonometry; result contains the canonical start and no heading. stepDistance=0 still performs every requested field query and heading calculation and retains repeated positions. angleScale=0 does not skip field validation or sampling. Prefix identity is conditional on both calls succeeding in the same target/runtime.
behavior.ownership: Path owns detached arrays and configuration. No writable field, renderer or external state is retained. pointAt returns a fresh pair; pointInto writes exactly two slots after all validation, never exposing internal arrays. headingAt returns a scalar. serialize returns detached canonical input for recomputation; toValues returns detached complete output_schema values and explicitly authorizes that extra materialization. Replay/getters/export do not sample the field or recompute movement. If serialize/toValues allocation fails, no new value is returned and the original path remains usable and unchanged. Failure does not invalidate or partially mutate the retained path.
behavior.access: Native steps() (Python steps property) is N. pointAt index domain0..N; headingAt0..N-1. Validate index as finite safe nonnegative integer <=9007199254740991 (booleans excluded), then access-specific bound. INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE. Optional pointInto checks index/domain then bounds then output and offset; offset must be finite nonnegative integral, with two writable binary64 slots. Invalid access leaves output unchanged. Float32 buffers are forbidden. In Java, the transport may use a typed int offset (unrepresentable/wrong-type calls are host call errors); dynamic-language offsets retain the stated runtime validation. This does not change valid pointInto behavior or index/bounds-before-storage error order.
behavior.native_forms: Java GradientPath2D.trace(Object config), pointAt(Object or long), headingAt(Object or long), pointInto(index,double[],offset), steps(), serialize(), toValues(). JavaScript gradientPath2D(config), pointAt, headingAt, pointInto, steps getter, serialize, toValues. Python gradient_path_2d(config), point_at, heading_at, point_into, steps property, serialize, to_values. No overload accepting arbitrary callbacks or host field objects in v0.1.0. Supplying an existing field serialize() value reuses its declared configuration.
behavior.native_types: Follow existing grid numeric conventions: Java Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double only; reject BigInteger/BigDecimal/custom Number before conversion. JavaScript passive object/Array input with number values; Python int/float but never bool, convert to finite binary64 after validating integer domains where applicable. Python huge integer conversion failure becomes INVALID_INPUT/INVALID_INDEX, not an uncaught conversion exception. Output pointInto accepts Java double[], JS Float64Array or writable ordinary Array, Python exact builtin list or array(d). Offset/count/index validation must precede narrowing. Active accessors/proxies and custom containers are not interchange data. Input containers: Java Map for records and exactly two-element List for pairs; arrays/PVector are not pair input carriers. Only passive container behavior belongs to interchange; active custom hooks are outside it. Python requires exact builtin dict records and exact builtin list pairs, rejecting custom Mapping/list subclasses and tuples. JS records have Object.prototype or null prototype and pairs are ordinary Array; class instances/typed-array pairs are not interchange input.
behavior.units: Planar caller-defined x/y coordinates, with heading0 advancing positive x and heading pi/2 positive y. Angles radians; host rendering decides whether positive y points down. FieldScale applies uniformly to both coordinate axes; offsets are lattice units. Step distance is coordinate units. Progress, envelope, perpendicular orientation and before/after anchor are caller choices.
behavior.numerics: Basic arithmetic IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even in stated order. Java/Android Math.sin/cos, JavaScript Math.sin/cos, Python math.sin/cos with no implicit angle normalization. Same-target identical inputs/runtime give exact replay and prefix. Cross-target coordinates/headings are checked under explicit per-case fixture tolerances, never a universal bit-identity or arbitrary-descriptor error-bound promise. Existing field algorithm remains exact for identical queries. Every completed zero output is canonical positive zero.
behavior.complexity: O(N) eager work and O(N) retained numeric storage; O(1) point/heading access and O(N) explicit detached value export. No per-step point object or command list. Source-range2000/16000 path measurements and declared example workloads required separately for each claimed runtime.
behavior.native_errors: Every library exception has code. Dynamic trace exceptions additionally expose stepIndex (Python step_index) and stage; these become error_detail:{stepIndex,stage} in interchange conformance reports. Static/access errors have no dynamic detail. Java may use a dedicated IllegalArgumentException subclass for validation and a dedicated ArithmeticException subclass for dynamic failures; JS Error subclasses and Python ValueError subclasses are native transport, not different semantic codes. Host allocation failure is not wrapped as a success or validation error.

operations.description: Composite same-sized straight ARGB8 rasters using an explicit scalar visibility mask.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Wrong shape/carriers, dimensions/product, unequal dimensions, pixel count/value, mask count/nonfinite/outside [0,1], null typed buffers.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Pixel index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Pixel index is representable but outside the retained output raster.

errorOrder: Follow behavior.validation; all configuration failures INVALID_INPUT.

behavior.input: Exactly source,destination,mask. Both raster records have exactly width,height,pixels. Positive integral dimensions; identical source/destination dimensions; exact pixel and mask counts. All pixels unsigned32; masks finite binary64 in [0,1]. No defaults.
behavior.compositing: For each pixel in row order: if mask == 0 or source alpha byte == 0, copy destination bits exactly. Otherwise let a=(sourceAlpha/255.0)*mask; b=destinationAlpha/255.0; t=1.0-a; u=b*t; v=a+u. If v == 0 (possible through underflow), output transparent black without division. Otherwise for each stored R,G,B byte pair s,d compute p=s*a; q=d*u; c=(p+q)/v. Output alpha byte Q(v*255.0), colors Q(c), where Q(x)=floor(min(255,max(0,x))+0.5). If quantized alpha is zero, output transparent black. Each stated arithmetic step is separately rounded binary64, ties-to-even; no FMA/reassociation or gamma conversion. The transparent-source/zero-mask identity branches precede transparent-black normalization and preserve hidden destination RGB.
behavior.ownership: The completed result owns a detached packed raster. It retains neither source pixels, destination pixels nor mask, and has no in-place form. Later caller mutation cannot affect the result. A failed call exposes no partial output.
behavior.access: width() and height() return dimensions. pixelAt(index) validates index as a finite safe nonnegative integer, then checks index < width*height; INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE. pixels() returns a detached int[] in Java (unsigned32 bit patterns), and toValues() returns detached {width,height,pixels}. Safe means at most 9007199254740991; negative zero is accepted as zero. pixelAt returns the Java int ARGB bit pattern; portable toValues pixels are unsigned32 numbers. Object indices accept only the same six numeric carriers as input.
behavior.numeric: IEEE binary64 arithmetic in stated order, one final byte quantization. Premultiplied working encoded RGB; no linear-light claim. Negative-zero mask equals zero.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.raster.MaskedComposite2D.compose(Object) and compose(int width,int height,int[] source,int[] destination,double[] mask). Result width(),height(),pixelAt(Object or long),pixels(),toValues(). Java implementation pending.
behavior.environment: No RNG, time, noise, host image, renderer, callback or mutable global state.
behavior.limits: width*height <= 2147483647, checked without signed32 overflow before allocation. Representation limit only; allocation failure is not INVALID_INPUT. O(width*height) time and owned output storage; no per-pixel allocation in typed kernel.
behavior.carriers: Object records are exact-key Map, arrays List. Numeric values accept only Byte,Short,Integer,Long,Float,Double; reject boolean, strings, BigInteger,BigDecimal, arbitrary Number subclasses. Dimensions and pixels integral within schema bounds, mask converts to finite double. Typed buffers non-null. Passive stable inputs required; concurrent input mutation outside contract.
behavior.validation: Object: top keys; source keys/dimensions/product/pixel count then values; destination keys/dimensions/product/matching dimensions/pixel count then values; mask count then values. Typed: dimensions/product; source count; destination count; mask count then values. Complete validation before output allocation. Failure exposes no partial result.

operations.description: Find the first closed-segment contact for each supplied directed query against supplied obstacles, retaining obstacle identity and explicit misses.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Static shape/carrier/domain failure.
errors.REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE: Interior selected contact cannot retain its distinction from a query endpoint; queryIndex and stage parameter or point.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Negative Java result index.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Nonnegative Java result index at or above size.

behavior.input: Exactly queries,obstacles,maxWork in a passive record. Validate keys; queries list and finite quadruples in order; obstacles list and finite quadruples in order; maxWork. Binary64 carriers only, no bool/string conversion. Java Byte,Short,Integer,Long,Float,Double only. Canonicalize signed zero. Validate all static input even when queries or obstacles empty. No defaults. Coordinates share caller units/origin/axes.
behavior.work: Let Q=queries.length,O=obstacles.length. Exact integer W=Q*O. WORK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED when W>maxWork after all static validation and before contact computation/output generation. W counts abstract pair tests, not arithmetic instructions, time or allocation. Counts are representational ceilings, not artistic ranges.
behavior.contact: Each query A+t(B-A) and obstacle C+u(D-C) is closed. Nonparallel intersection qualifies iff exact t,u in[0,1]. Parallel noncollinear pairs miss. Collinear pairs intersect in a closed query-parameter interval: choose its least t. A zero-length query has t=0 iff its point belongs to the obstacle; a point obstacle may be contacted. Empty intersection misses. No automatic self/same-origin filtering. All predicates and ordering use exact rational values of supplied binary64 inputs.
behavior.selection: Select smallest exact t per query, ties by smallest supplied obstacle ordinal. Obstacle orientation does not affect contact location. Query orientation does. Return one entry per query in original order: null for miss or record obstacleIndex,t,point. No mutation or feedback between queries; later obstacles are not shortened by earlier queries. Overlap extent is not returned.
behavior.rounding: After selecting contact round exact t and each exact A+t(B-A) coordinate once to binary64 nearest-even; normalize zero. Exact t=0/1 preserves corresponding normalized input endpoint. For exact0<t<1 throw REPRESENTATION_COLLAPSE stage parameter if rounded t is0or1; otherwise stage point if rounded point equals either query endpoint. Include queryIndex and stage. Check queries in input order; parameter before point. No partial output. Exact endpoint contacts including point queries are valid. Rounded point may lie slightly off exact obstacle; no painted-footprint guarantee.
behavior.ownership: Inputs not retained or mutated. Result owns contacts; exports detached data. No RNG,time,renderer or host objects. Native allocation failure remains host failure.
behavior.complexity: O(Q*O) exact geometric pair tests plus exact arithmetic bit costs; O(Q+O) captured input and O(Q) result storage; no per-pair retained result.
behavior.access: Java reference exposes static find(Object configuration), size(), hitAt(long index) and toValues(). hitAt returns null for miss or immutable Contact with obstacleIndex,t,x,y primitive fields. Negative indices produce INVALID_INDEX; index>=size produces INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE. toValues returns independently owned output-schema records/lists. No mutable array accessor is necessary for a single contact. Java ContactException extends IllegalArgumentException with public final code, queryIndex and stage; queryIndex=-1 and stage=null except representation collapse. Contact fields are immutable primitive values; constructors are private.

operations.description: Retain an attempt-bounded connected path whose accepted proposals remain within a strict scalar band around the starting noise value.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed static carrier/key/value, nonfinite value or out-of-domain static field.
errors.TRACE_QUERY_INVALID: Dynamic field coordinate invalid; includes attemptIndex and query stage.
errors.TRACE_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: Dynamic nonfinite heading, displacement or endpoint; includes attemptIndex and stage.
errors.VERTEX_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: An accepted append would exceed maxVertices; includes attemptIndex and append stage.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Index exceeds retained point or heading range.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: pointInto destination or offset cannot hold two binary64 values.

behavior.input: Validate passive input outer shape and exact keys, then field exactly {seed:uint32}, start exactly two finite binary64 coordinates x then y, heading finite binary64 radians without normalization, seed integer0..4294967295, attempts integer0..2147483647, stepDistance finite binary64 >=0, fieldScale finite binary64 including negative and zero, fieldOffset exactly two finite binary64 field coordinates, tolerance finite binary64 >=0, and maxVertices integer1..1073741823, in that order. Reject booleans, null, strings and arbitrary Number classes. All static failures are INVALID_INPUT. There are no defaults, recommended ranges or host fields/callbacks. Canonicalize -0 to +0 before computation and detached configuration export.
behavior.rng: Portable xoshiro128**1.1 private to each call. Zero-extend uint32 seed to uint64 SplitMix64 state. Twice advance state by0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 modulo2^64; z=state; z=(z xor(z>>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9 mod2^64; z=(z xor(z>>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb mod2^64; q=z xor(z>>>31). Pack q0/q1 as s0=low32(q0),s1=high32(q0),s2=low32(q1),s3=high32(q1). next output=rotl32(s1*5 mod2^32,7)*9 mod2^32; then t=s1<<9 mod2^32; sequentially s2 xor=s0; s3 xor=s1; s1 xor=s2; s0 xor=s3; s2 xor=t; s3=rotl32(s3,11), all words uint32. Map output to u=unsigned_u32/4294967296 exactly in[0,1). State is private/discarded and never shares Processing/source/background/palette state. The all-zero state is unreachable and an internal invariant.
behavior.transition: Use fdlibm5.3 binary64 sin/cos as provided by Java StrictMath; no caller angle reduction. All basic operators round separately to binary64, with no FMA or reassociation. HALF_PI=0x1.921fb54442d18p0; decimal .1 and .2 mean nearest binary64 values. C(v,stage) raises TRACE_ARITHMETIC_INVALID with attemptIndex and stage if v is nonfinite. Q(x,y,prefix) evaluates qx=x*fieldScale, checks that product finite, then qx=qx+offsetX, checks that final value is finite and -9007199254740991 <= qx < 9007199254740991; then does the same qy with the x/y prefix stages. An invalid product or final value raises TRACE_QUERY_INVALID. Query existing field.sample(qx,qy), whose finite [0,1] output is guaranteed. After static validation retain start and heading. If attempts=0 return immediately with no RNG draws, field sample, coordinate transform or trig. Otherwise attemptIndex=-1; level=Q(startX,startY,start_query); then create private RNG. For attemptIndex 0..attempts-1: u0=U(); low=(-HALF_PI)*u0; u1=U(); high=HALF_PI*u1; span=high-low; u2=U(); delta=span*u2; turn=low+delta; proposal=C(heading+turn,proposal_heading); dx=C(stepDistance*fdlibmCos(proposal),delta_x); nx=C(x+dx,position_x); dy=C(stepDistance*fdlibmSin(proposal),delta_y); ny=C(y+dy,position_y); value=Q(nx,ny,candidate_query); u3=U(); driftProduct=.2*u3; drift=-.1+driftProduct; rejectionHeading=C(heading+drift,rejection_heading); difference=value-level; bandError=abs(difference). If bandError < tolerance, fail VERTEX_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with attemptIndex and append stage when size==maxVertices, then canonicalize nx,ny,proposal, append point and heading, update x,y,heading and accepted. Otherwise canonicalize rejectionHeading into heading and increment rejected. Every completed attempt consumes four draws; rejection drift is calculated and validated even on acceptance. No retry, early stop, boundary handling or partial result.
behavior.canonicalization: Every stored coordinate and heading is canonical positive zero when equal to zero. Canonicalize updated x, y and heading before they feed the next attempt; do not canonicalize every temporary. Subnormal values and arithmetic underflow are permitted, with no flush-to-zero profile. The difference of two field samples cannot overflow. Trig and field are evaluated for zero distance. Resource failure is tested only for an actually accepted append, after candidate query and rejection-heading checks.
behavior.storage: O(attempts) work and O(accepted) retained numeric payload, 24 bytes per accepted move plus 16-byte starting coordinates excluding headers/capacity. Grow bounded packed arrays lazily; never preallocate maxVertices, retain rejected coordinates or create per-attempt objects. Resource failure is checked only for an actually accepted append, after candidate query and rejection-heading checks. Host allocation failures remain host errors.
behavior.native_surface: Java reference class is org.procedurals.paths.NoiseBandPath2D with static trace(Object). size(), attempts(), accepted(), rejected() return int; pointAt(Object/long) returns new double[2]; pointInto(Object/long,double[],int) writes two coordinates; headingAt(Object/long) returns the proposal heading for accepted segment i; serialize() returns detached validated configuration; toValues() returns exactly {positions:[[x,y],...],headings:[...],attempts,accepted,rejected}. No mutable state, shared RNG, drawing, implicit seed layout or incremental execution API.
behavior.access: For point and heading access, reject nonfinite, negative, fractional or >9007199254740991 index as INVALID_INDEX; a valid index >=size (point) or >=accepted (heading) is INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE. pointInto validates index before output; null/insufficient double[] or negative/overflowing offset gives INVALID_OUTPUT with no writes. Failed queries leave the result usable.
behavior.native_representations: Java interchange: passive Map records and List pairs; only Byte,Short,Integer,Long,Float,Double numeric carriers. Reject BigInteger,BigDecimal,custom Number and booleans before conversion. pointInto accepts double[] and int offset; no partial writes. No arbitrary field/callback inputs. JSON ordinary records/arrays define future portable interchange; no runtime support is implied.
