behavior.normative_transition: design/operations/noise-band-path-contract.md; transition and ordered arithmetic there are normative together with this catalog. No new host-dependent semantics may be inferred.
behavior.numeric_details: Canonicalize input and stored coordinate/heading zeros to +0 before subsequent use; intermediate signed zeros remain IEEE754. Subnormals and underflow are permitted; no flush-to-zero. Trig and field queries execute even at zero stepDistance. Four draws per completed attempt even when bounds coincide or tolerance is zero; dynamic errors stop before later draws. Query product is checked finite only; final product+offset must also meet lattice bounds. Error detail is exactly {attemptIndex,stage}, with -1 for initial query and zero-based attempts thereafter; static and access errors have no dynamic detail.
behavior.ownership: Copy input configuration; construct privately; serialize and toValues deeply detached. Caller modifications before/after export cannot alter retained path. Host allocation errors remain host errors and no partial result escapes.

operations.description: Generate ordered retained cardinal cell paths whose cells are claimed by one call-local occupancy set.

dimensions.description: [columns, rows] integer lattice dimensions; origin is north-west, x grows east and y grows south.

starts.description: Ordered start-cell pairs. Duplicates are valid sequential occupancy outcomes.

maxSteps.description: Maximum successful cardinal moves after each available start.

random.description: Exactly one private-stream carrier: uint32 seed or nonzero [s0,s1,s2,s3] uint32 state.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed static carrier/key/value, out-of-domain coordinate/limit, seed/state carrier or forbidden all-zero supplied state.
errors.WORK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: All static fields are valid but starts.length*(maxSteps+1) exceeds maxCells.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Path or cell index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: A representable path or cell index exceeds its retained range.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: cellInto destination or offset cannot hold two int values.

behavior.input: Input has exactly dimensions, starts, maxSteps, maxCells and random. Static validation order is: outer passive record/keys; dimensions pair then columns then rows; starts outer List/length, then each pair and its x then y in increasing start index; maxSteps; maxCells; random record/keys, then its sole seed or state carrier and state words in increasing index. Every numeric carrier is finite integral in its stated domain and never bool. Each start must be within its corresponding half-open dimension. State [0,0,0,0] is INVALID_INPUT. Complete all static validation before comparing capacity, initializing the stream, claiming occupancy, allocating output-sized storage or mutating caller data. Then calculate starts.length*(maxSteps+1) with exact checked wide integer arithmetic; if it exceeds maxCells, fail WORK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. No defaults.
behavior.generation: Use one call-local sparse occupancy set and process starts in input order. An occupied start appends [] and occupied-start and consumes no word. Otherwise append and claim the start. If maxSteps is zero, append step-limit before enumerating neighbours. For each remaining successful move, enumerate in-bounds unoccupied candidates in north, east, south, west order. No candidates appends blocked without a word. Otherwise consume one word, select one candidate, append it and claim it. Reaching maxSteps successful moves appends step-limit. There are no retries, proposals with replacement, random starts, truncation or partial output.
behavior.rng: Portable xoshiro128**1.1 private to each call. Zero-extend uint32 seed to uint64 SplitMix64 state. Twice advance state by0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 modulo2^64; z=state; z=(z xor(z>>>30))*0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9 mod2^64; z=(z xor(z>>>27))*0x94d049bb133111eb mod2^64; q=z xor(z>>>31). Pack q0/q1 as s0=low32(q0),s1=high32(q0),s2=low32(q1),s3=high32(q1). next output=rotl32(s1*5 mod2^32,7)*9 mod2^32; then t=s1<<9 mod2^32; sequentially s2 xor=s0; s3 xor=s1; s1 xor=s2; s0 xor=s3; s2 xor=t; s3=rotl32(s3,11), all words uint32. A supplied state bypasses seed expansion. For available count c in1..4, choose floor(unsigned_u32*c/4294967296); this consumes exactly one word, including c=1. This discrete mapping is the contract and does not assert equal mathematical probability where c does not divide2^32. Blocked and occupied-start paths consume no word.
behavior.integer_layout: Coordinates are signed int32 values; valid dimensions ensure every emitted coordinate and cardinal neighbour calculation is representable. Retain two signed int32 coordinate scalars per emitted cell in growable owned packed storage. maxCells<=1073741823 keeps total two-coordinate scalar storage signed-int-indexable. Do not dense-allocate by dimensions, preallocate maxCells, or allocate per-cell output objects during generation. maxCells is a representation admission ceiling, not an actual output, latency, memory or artistic guarantee. Host allocation failures are host failures and never translated into operation errors.
behavior.ownership: Inputs are never mutated or retained. Occupancy, packed output and stream state are local to one eager call. The result owns detached storage. Each materialized JSON path/cell/state carrier and each native accessor carrier is fresh; changing it cannot affect the result. Exporting/read access never advances the stream. A rejected configuration exposes no result and no partial output.
behavior.native_surface: Java reference class is org.procedurals.paths.OccupiedLatticePaths2D with static generate(Object config). Public accessors are int pathCount(); int pathLengthAt(Object path) and pathLengthAt(long path); int[] cellAt(Object path,Object cell) and cellAt(long path,long cell); void cellInto(Object path,Object cell,int[] output,int offset) and cellInto(long path,long cell,int[] output,int offset); String completionReasonAt(Object path) and completionReasonAt(long path); long[] randomState(); and Map<String,Object> toValues(). No mixed path/cell overload exists. randomState returns a fresh long[4], each 0..4294967295; cellAt returns fresh int[2]. The only public operation exception is nested LatticeException extends IllegalArgumentException with final String code. Host resource exceptions remain host exceptions.
behavior.access: All path/cell indices are finite safe nonnegative integers no greater than9007199254740991, with booleans excluded; integral floating carriers are accepted where a host supports them. For cellAt/cellInto, validate in this exact field order: path numeric domain, path range, cell numeric domain, cell range, then destination. An out-of-range path therefore wins over an invalid cell carrier; an invalid cell carrier wins over destination validation only after the path is in range. Thus empty occupied-start paths have no valid cell index. cellInto requires an int[] with two writable slots starting at a finite nonnegative integral offset and writes both only after every validation succeeds; any failure leaves every destination slot unchanged.
behavior.complexity: For admitted inputs, O(starts.length + emitted cells) retained storage and O(starts.length + successfulMoves) transition work, with at most four candidate checks per successful-move iteration. Sparse occupancy is O(emitted cells). path/cell scalar reads are O(1); toValues is O(starts.length + emitted cells) detached materialization, including empty occupied-start entries.
environment: explicit private xoshiro128**1.1 seed or state
behavior.exclusions: No renderer, drawing commands, grid metric, palette, style stream, session, callback, graph, maze/route guarantee, global occupancy, retained continuation object, host RNG, clock or noise is consumed. Guagua's unrestricted revisiting walk is deferred and is not this operation.

operations.description: Retain supplied circles in order when their radius-dependent exclusion test permits them alongside earlier accepted circles.

centres.description: Ordered candidate centre pairs; length must equal radii length.

radii.description: One positive radius per centre, in the same coordinate unit.

separationScale.description: Multiplier on summed radii;1 permits tangency, below1 permits overlap, above1 reserves size-relative clearance.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, including wrong shape, unsupported passive carrier, bool numeric, unequal centre/radius lengths, nonpositive radius or separationScale, or proposal cardinality above the representation bound.
errors.PLACEMENT_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: Dynamic nonfinite pair arithmetic or specified pair underflow; candidateIndex and named pair stage, no output.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite nonnegative safe integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Valid index is outside0..size-1.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: pointInto destination or offset lacks two writable binary64 slots.

behavior.layout: A placement result privately retains 2*N binary64 centre coordinates, N binary64 radii and N integer original proposal indices, where N is accepted count. Apply proposal-count ceiling1073741823 statically to seeded attempts or explicit input length, so even accepting every proposal fits2*N<=2147483647. This is a shared packed-array/index representation bound, not an allocation, latency or useful artistic range guarantee. Capacity growth must be capped at this representation ceiling without integer overflow. Host allocation failure returns no result and remains a host resource exception, never INVALID_INPUT or partial successful output.
behavior.acceptance: Visit proposals in original order i=0..attempts-1. For each, visit retained circles in their acceptance order. Compute dx=round64(x-oldX), dy=round64(y-oldY), xx=round64(dx*dx), yy=round64(dy*dy), squared=round64(xx+yy), sumR=round64(r+oldR), threshold=round64(sumR*separationScale), limitSquared=round64(threshold*threshold), in that exact order with validation immediately after each stage. Reject the proposal at the first pair where squared<limitSquared and skip its remaining pairs. Equality is accepted. If no pair rejects, append canonical centre, positive radius and original index. The first valid proposal is accepted without pair arithmetic. Seeded generation and explicit filtering feed exactly this same internal kernel; no duplicated predicate or implicit sorting.
behavior.pair_validation: For each computed pair stage require finite binary64. Stages in order: difference_x, difference_y, square_x, square_y, distance_squared, radius_sum, threshold, threshold_squared. Also fail square_x when dx!=0 and xx==0; fail square_y when dy!=0 and yy==0; fail threshold when threshold<=0 (positive operands must not underflow to zero); fail threshold_squared when limitSquared==0. These conservative guards reject nonzero square underflow and collapsed positive exclusion, without an arbitrary coordinate envelope. Failure code PLACEMENT_ARITHMETIC_INVALID includes candidateIndex=i and stage. Discard the entire internal accepted prefix and return no result. Do not report the compared retained index. A rejected proposal does not evaluate later pair stages or remaining retained pairs.
behavior.ownership: Result owns detached accepted arrays only. Inputs must not be mutated concurrently with either eager call; active getters/proxies/custom hooks are outside the passive interchange contract. Complete the full static validation pass before allocating result-sized retained storage or starting pair work. A full-input snapshot is not required. Do not retain caller-owned arrays or persistent rejected-proposal copies. Getter returns and toValues are detached. toValues returns exactly output_schema and explicitly authorizes additional O(N) materialization. Allocation failure in a fresh pointAt/point_at pair or toValues/to_values materialization returns no new value and leaves the original retained result usable and unchanged. The result has no serialize/toJSON/config replay API: callers retain their input configuration; accepted geometry is not a reconstruction of the rejected proposal sequence.
behavior.access: Native size() and attempts() (JavaScript/Python properties) return accepted N and original proposal count. Rejected count is attempts-size; do not add count aliases. pointAt/point_at returns a fresh two-number centre, radiusAt/radius_at returns one radius, sourceIndexAt/source_index_at returns original proposal index. All indices require finite nonnegative safe integer<=9007199254740991, never bool; integral floating indices are accepted. INVALID_INDEX precedes INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE (index>=N). pointInto/point_into checks index validity and bound before destination/offset. Then require writable binary64 space for exactly two slots and a finite nonnegative integral offset; otherwise INVALID_OUTPUT. Never mutate any destination slot on failure. Float32 output buffers are forbidden. Java may use typed int offset; wrong-type/unrepresentable host calls are host-call errors, not different interchange semantics. Java pointInto has a required typed int offset and returns void. JavaScript pointInto(index,out,offset=0) returns the supplied out destination. Python point_into(index,out,offset=0) returns None. These are native transport conventions; all write the same two coordinates and preserve the same failure ordering.
behavior.native_types: Follow existing grid numeric conventions: Java Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double only; reject BigInteger/BigDecimal/custom Number before conversion. JavaScript passive object/Array input with number values; Python int/float but never bool, convert to finite binary64 after validating integer domains where applicable. Python huge integer conversion failure becomes INVALID_INPUT/INVALID_INDEX, not an uncaught conversion exception. Output pointInto accepts Java double[], JS Float64Array or writable ordinary Array, Python exact builtin list or array(d). Offset/count/index validation must precede narrowing. Active accessors/proxies and custom containers are not interchange data. Input containers: Java Map for records and exactly two-element List for pairs; arrays/PVector are not pair input carriers. Only passive container behavior belongs to interchange; active custom hooks are outside it. Python requires exact builtin dict records and exact builtin list pairs, rejecting custom Mapping/list subclasses and tuples. JS records have Object.prototype or null prototype and pairs are ordinary Array; class instances/typed-array pairs are not interchange input.
behavior.numerics: IEEE754 binary64 round-to-nearest ties-to-even for every basic operation in the stated order. No FMA, reassociation, sqrt/hypot substitute, epsilon, binary32 conversion or host transcendental in the core. Normalize every zero input coordinate and completed zero output coordinate to positive zero. Radius and scale must be strictly positive. Compare core output coordinates/radii by exact binary64 bits and all counts/source indices/errors exactly across targets; do not tolerate topology differences. This is a checked floating predicate, not an exact real-number geometry guarantee. Supplied radial points are caller data: cross-host trigonometry used to construct them is outside this contract.
behavior.units: Caller-defined planar centre coordinates and radii in the same length unit. A radius is half a circle diameter. No canvas, axis orientation or renderer is implicit; host drawing may use y downward. separationScale is dimensionless, multiplying summed radii:1 permits computed tangency, below1 permits geometric overlap, above1 adds size-relative clearance. It is not a fixed pixel gap. The filter has no containment domain.
behavior.complexity: O(P*A) pair work, at worst O(P^2), for P proposals and up to A accepted circles; O(A) retained primitive storage and O(1) accessor work. Explicit filtering also statically validates all P records before pair work. Seeded generation streams candidates and retains no all-proposal array. Eager invocation authorizes finite work; no universal real-time or saturation guarantee. Any future acceleration must preserve outputs AND defined failure behavior/order, not merely typical placements.
behavior.native_errors: Validation/access exceptions have code. PLACEMENT_ARITHMETIC_INVALID additionally exposes candidateIndex (Python candidate_index) and stage, emitted as error_detail:{candidateIndex,stage} by conformance runners. Static INVALID_INPUT and accessor errors have no dynamic detail. Java validation errors may subclass IllegalArgumentException and arithmetic errors ArithmeticException; JS Error and Python ValueError subclasses are transport. Host resource failures are not converted to validation errors or partial success.
behavior.input: Input has exactly centres, radii, separationScale. Validate outer passive record/keys; centres Array/List length0..1073741823; radii Array/List and equal length; separationScale finite positive; then for i=0..P-1 validate centre pair and finite x/y, then positive finite radius, in that order. Booleans are never numbers. Validate EVERY explicit proposal before allocating result-sized retained storage or starting pair work, including proposals that would later be rejected. Normalize coordinate zeros; explicit input must not mutate during this synchronous eager call. Do not retain rejected input after return. Empty input still validates scale and returns empty arrays with attempts0.
behavior.native_forms: Java org.procedurals.sampling.CirclePlacements2D.filter(Object config) returns CirclePlacements2D, with size(),attempts(),pointAt(Object or long),pointInto(index,double[],int offset),radiusAt(Object or long),sourceIndexAt(Object or long),toValues(). JavaScript orderedCircleFilter2D(config) returns result with size/attempts getters, pointAt,pointInto,radiusAt,sourceIndexAt,toValues. Python ordered_circle_filter_2d(config) returns result with size/attempts properties, point_at,point_into,radius_at,source_index_at,to_values. No result serialize/toJSON or count aliases. Both operations return the same result type/semantics.
behavior.environment: No RNG, noise, time, renderer, asset, lifecycle or trigonometric input. Supplied circle values and order plus separationScale fully determine the result.
behavior.degenerate: Coincident or collinear centres are valid inputs; the ordered predicate decides acceptance. Radius0/negative, negative or zero separationScale, nonfinite values and mismatched lengths are INVALID_INPUT. A tiny positive radius can be retained as the first/only circle; a later pair may fail the specified arithmetic guards. Below1 scale permits overlap. No hidden clamping, containment, deduplication, sorting or geometric tolerance.

operations.description: Ordered greedy filtering of supplied strictly convex polygon outlines using exact inclusive intersection; retained geometry and original proposal indices.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed config/container/carrier/nonfinite coordinate or representational count overflow.
errors.INVALID_POLYGON: Finite structurally valid polygon is not a strict convex cycle.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Invalid result polygon or vertex index.

behavior.ordering: All proposals validated in order before greedy filtering; retained order and vertex cycle preserved.
behavior.numerics: Finite normalized binary64 coordinates as exact dyadic reals for geometric signs. Inclusive symmetric contact/containment; no epsilon.
behavior.ownership: Detached immutable retained geometry/source indices; fresh toValues.
behavior.complexity: O(V+N) storage; O(sum m_i²) validation and worst-case O(sum compared m_i*m_j) pair work; cached broad phase and certified exact fallback.

operations.description: Generate an owned indexed-triangle radial surface from a caller-supplied ordered local axial radius profile, angular subdivision, independent endpoint closures, and explicit face bound. It computes retained local geometry, topology metadata, and flat unit normals only.

profile.description: Ordered local [z,radius] pairs. z strictly increases; endpoint radii are nonnegative and interior radii are strictly positive. Only the two-point profile whose two endpoint radii are both zero is invalid; a P>=3 profile may have poles at both endpoints.

slices.description: Angular cell count. This upper value is a representational ceiling, not an encouraged resolution or allocation guarantee.

capStart.description: Request a fan cap at the first positive-radius profile ring. A zero-radius start pole already closes itself.

capEnd.description: Request a fan cap at the last positive-radius profile ring. A zero-radius end pole already closes itself.

maxFaces.description: Required caller face-work limit. Its maximum is a signed-int packed-representation ceiling, not a practical-work or artistic recommendation.

positions.description: Owned local [x,y,z] vertex positions in canonical profile-ring/pole then cap-centre order.

normals.description: Owned local flat unit [x,y,z] normals aligned one-to-one with triangles.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Malformed/nonfinite/out-of-domain static input, including wrong passive carrier/keys/shape, bool numeric, profile length below2, non-increasing axial coordinate, endpoint negative radius, nonpositive interior radius, the two-point profile with both endpoint radii zero, slices outside3..715827881, nonboolean cap, or maxFaces outside1..715827881.
errors.FACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: Complete static input is valid but exact preallocation face count F exceeds required maxFaces. No geometry/RNG/output allocation or partial result occurs.
errors.MESH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID: Generated face has nonfinite edge component, zero edge scale, or zero rounded scaled cross. error_detail has faceIndex and edge,edge_scale,or cross_scale stage; no output is returned.
errors.INVALID_INDEX: Index is not a finite safe nonnegative integer.
errors.INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE: Representable index is outside the requested retained array range.
errors.INVALID_OUTPUT: An Into destination/offset does not provide three writable slots of the required native element type.

errorOrder: INVALID_INPUT during complete static input validation
FACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED after static validation and exact count calculation, before geometry allocation
MESH_ARITHMETIC_INVALID during canonical face-normal traversal after topology/positions are generated
INVALID_INDEX, INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, INVALID_OUTPUT during retained-result access in that order

behavior.input: Input has exactly profile,slices,capStart,capEnd,maxFaces. Static validation order is outer passive record/exact keys; profile outer List and length; each profile pair in increasing list order, pair shape then z then radius, including z monotonicity and endpoint/interior radius constraints; the special two-point/both-poles rejection; slices; capStart; capEnd; maxFaces. Every accepted number is finite binary64 and never bool. Integral slices/maxFaces carriers validate their stated domains before narrowing. Normalize accepted zeros to +0. No sort, resampling, implicit profile, callback, default, or later-field short circuit. Complete static validation, including unused later profile rows, precedes count capacity, allocation and geometry.
behavior.counts_and_layout: Let P=profile length, S=slices, K=number of positive-radius profile points, Z=number of endpoint poles, and C=number of requested caps whose endpoint ring is positive. V=K*S+Z+C. Each positive-to-positive side band emits2*S triangles; each pole-adjacent side band emitsS; each requested positive-ring cap emitsS. Compute F with exact wide integer arithmetic after static validation and before geometry allocation. FACE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED if F>maxFaces. The accepted count proof in design/operations/cp7-count-bounds.md establishes V<=F+1 for the admitted domain, including P>=3 double-pole profiles; P<=2147483647 and S,maxFaces<=715827881 keep count expressions within signed64 arithmetic and retained triples addressable by signed-int packed storage. These values do not guarantee allocation success, latency, or a useful artistic range. Host resource allocation failure returns no result and is never INVALID_INPUT or partial success. Core retained work/storage is O(P*S), indexed reads O(1), detached export O(F+V).
behavior.topology: Local axis is Z. Angles increase from +X toward +Y. Set TAU=6.283185307179586 and evaluate theta=(TAU*cell)/slices in that order; position=(radius*cos(theta),radius*sin(theta),z) using named-target binary64 trigonometry. Positive rings append S vertices in input-profile then increasing-cell order. A zero-radius endpoint appends exactly one (0,0,z) pole; no 2pi seam vertex is evaluated or stored. Append requested cap centres after all profile positions, start before end. Visit side bands in input order then cells increasing with next=(cell+1) moduloS. Breadth-first expansion phase: an inactive parent consumes no draw; an active parent samples scale then each slot gate. A failed gate cannot raise capacity or child arithmetic. Each lengthScale and turn interval must also satisfy its first endpoint<=its second endpoint; this cross-field requirement is INVALID_INPUT and cannot be expressed by the Draft 2020-12 pair schema alone. Visit parents in increasing retained index order, including children appended earlier by preceding parents. A parent whose generation is outside rules consumes no units. Otherwise consume exactly one unit for that rule shared per-parent scale, including when its slots list is empty. For each slot in declared order consume exactly one gate unit even when probability is0 or1; it succeeds iff gate<probability. A failure consumes no angle. On success, check maxSegments before another draw or child arithmetic, consume exactly one angle unit, compute/validate and append the child immediately, then increment the parent child count. Children are visited only later through the growing retained list; no recursive descent, retry, invisible/style draw or terminal shrink draw occurs.

Former leaves may acquire children, so childCounts, terminal membership, full output and output-array prefix equality are not promised. Changing only a later rule preserves earlier-level geometry under the same condition. A rule expression normalized by total depth is a changed existing rule and forfeits this guarantee. Altering early slots/gates may shift subsequent stream consumption and has no broader locality promise.

Otherwise, when a and b have strictly opposite signs, raw=round64(round64(a*round64(1-t))+round64(b*t)); otherwise raw=round64(a+round64(round64(b-a)*t)). Each arithmetic operator below rounds separately to binary64. C(value,stage) fails

arguments evaluate left-to-right. Constants are nearest binary64 decimal values.
U() is one unsigned xoshiro output divided by4294967296. PI=0x1.921fb54442d18p1.
R(lo,hi) returns lo without U when lo>=hi; otherwise lo+((hi-lo)*U()). All R bounds
below are finite in[0,3] or[-.1,.1], so their arithmetic cannot overflow. Upper-bound
rounding is accepted, not retried. First-cut selection is min(2,floor(3*U())).

For attempt=0..attempts-1:

 sx,sy,ex,ey = selected current endpoints
 dx=C(ex-sx,"difference_x"); dy=C(ey-sy,"difference_y")
 xx=C(dx*dx,"square_x"); yy=C(dy*dy,"square_y")
 squared=C(xx+yy,"squared_length"); length=correctlyRoundedSqrt(squared)
 heading=fdlibmAtan2(dy,dx)
 if length<minCutLength: skips++; continue
 fraction=R(R(.6,.7),R(0,.8))
 if divided[index]: fraction=fraction*.4
 remainder=length*(1-fraction)  # finite: fraction in[0,.8],length finite

   a=R(0,1.2)*R(.2,1); a=C(a*firstCutAngleScale,"spread_positive")

   l2=C(remainder*R(.9,1.2),"length_straight")

   h1=C(heading-b,"heading_negative")
   h2=C(heading+R(-.1,.1),"heading_straight")
   choice=min(2,floor(3*U()))
